pain_points: Git CLI on mobile is impossible. There's no native way to unzip a project folder, stage changes, and push commits from your phone — until now.
If you've ever tried to use Termux or SSH just to push a quick fix from your phone, you know how painful it is. Typing git commands on a touchscreen keyboard is a nightmare.
Most developers assume you need a laptop to use Git. That's not true anymore. You can unzip, edit, and push directly from your mobile device in under 30 seconds.
You're at dinner, on the train, or lying in bed — and you need to push a fix to your repo RIGHT NOW. Opening a laptop isn't an option. Here's how to do it from your phone.

faq_pairs.q: Can I really push to {platform} from my {device}?
faq_pairs.a: Yes. {AppName} handles the entire Git workflow — unzip, stage, commit, and push — directly from your mobile browser. No terminal required.

faq_pairs.q: Do I need to install an app?
faq_pairs.a: No. {AppName} is a Progressive Web App. Just visit the site on your {device}, add it to your home screen, and you're ready to push code in seconds.
Absolutely. We use OAuth directly with {platform}. We never store your password or SSH keys. Your credentials never touch our servers.

faq_pairs.q: Does it work with private repositories?
faq_pairs.a: Yes. Once you authenticate with {platform} via OAuth, you can push to any public or private repository you have access to.

faq_pairs.q: What file types can I upload?
faq_pairs.a: You can upload and unzip .zip, .tar.gz, and .rar files containing any project files — HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, React, and more.
